items.summary: A good problem to have for a $1,600 smartphone.
items.body:

Motorola Signature 27 demand pushes US delivery dates into December

A good problem to have for a $1,600 smartphone.

•

Nov 25, 2026 — 1:11 AM ET

•

•

Stephen Radochia / Android Authority

Add Android Authority on Google:

Preferred Source

Google Discover

TL;DR

• Motorola lists a December 8 shipping date for the Signature 27, while Best Buy shows December 11 deliveries or no stock.

• Motorola has confirmed that higher-than-expected demand is behind the revised shipping timelines.

• Some early buyers could still receive their phones ahead of the November 26 US retail launch.

A $1,600 Motorola phone proving harder to get hold of than expected isn’t something many would have predicted a year ago. Yet that’s the situation facing the Motorola Signature 27, the company’s big-ticket challenger to Samsung, Google, and Apple in the US. Demand has exceeded Motorola’s expectations, and new buyers may have to wait until December for their phones to arrive.

As spotted by 9to5Google, shipping dates for the Signature 27 have slipped into December. Motorola confirmed to the publication that demand has exceeded its initial expectations, resulting in revised shipping timelines for some orders.

We’re excited by the strong consumer response of the new motorola signature 27, with demand exceeding our initial expectations. As a result, some orders may experience updated shipping timelines. Our teams are working to meet demand and get devices to customers as quickly as possible.

Our own checks show that Motorola’s website currently lists a December 8 shipping date, while availability at Best Buy appears to vary by location. Some of us are seeing a December 11 shipping date with no in-store pickup option, while others can no longer pre-order the phone and are instead greeted with a “Notify Me” button.

However, not everyone is facing a longer wait. Some Signature 27 buyers are still on course to receive their units in time for the official retail launch. This suggests at least some early pre-orders are moving through the fulfillment process.

The Signature 27 was originally slated to go on sale in the US on November 26, following a week of pre-orders. Meanwhile, European sales began on November 16, and Motorola has now confirmed a December 9 launch in India.

What’s particularly interesting about the demand is that Motorola isn’t undercutting the competition this time. At $1,600, the Signature 27 is asking buyers to part with a serious chunk of change. Granted, a 7,000mAh battery, Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 processor, and 200MP telephoto camera make for a compelling hardware package. Motorola’s seven-year software support commitment, despite its caveats, also makes the asking price a little easier to stomach.

For years, Motorola’s biggest challenge in the US flagship market was giving people a reason to buy its phones over a Galaxy or Pixel. With the Signature 27, its immediate challenge appears to be getting enough phones into buyers’ hands.

• T-Mobile’s Black Friday deals include the Galaxy S26 Plus, Pixel 11 Pro, Galaxy S26, Razr Fold, and Razr Plus for free with a trade-in or a new line on a qualifying plan.

• Metro by T-Mobile is giving away the Galaxy A37 5G to switchers who join its $40 plan, while T-Mobile’s 12 Days of Magenta accessory deals run from December 1 to 12 in the T-Life app.

• The device discounts are paid back as up to 36 monthly bill credits, which stop if you cancel or pay off your phone early.

T-Mobile has announced its Black Friday deals for 2026, and the headline offers are free flagships from Samsung, Google, and Motorola. The carrier says the deals add up to over $1,000 in savings on select devices across T-Mobile, Metro by T-Mobile, and T-Mobile for Business.

Here are the phones you can get “on Us” at T-Mobile, either by trading in an eligible device or by adding a new line on a qualifying plan:

• Samsung Galaxy S26 Plus: Up to $1,200 off. New lines need Experience Beyond or a T-Mix plan with three Picks.

• Google Pixel 11 Pro: Up to $1,100 off. New lines need Experience More, Experience Beyond, or a T-Mix plan with two Picks.

• Samsung Galaxy S26: Up to $1,000 off, with the same plan requirements as the Pixel 11 Pro.

• Motorola Razr Fold: Up to $1,800 off. New lines need Experience Beyond or a T-Mix plan with two Picks.

• Motorola Razr Plus: Up to $1,100 off. New lines need Experience More, Experience Beyond, or a T-Mix plan with two Picks.

There’s also a family offer for switchers. If you move to T-Mobile on T-Mix Standard, you get four lines for $25 per line per month with AutoPay, plus four Pixel 11 phones on Us with four Picks, either by trading in four eligible devices or by activating four new lines.

Wearables and tablets are part of T-Mobile’s Black Friday sale, too. When you add a watch line on a qualifying plan, T-Mobile will give you the Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 (up to $700 off, starting November 25), the Pixel Watch 5 (up to $500 off), or the Galaxy Watch9 (up to $430 off) on Us. The Galaxy Tab A11 Plus 5G and the Revvl Tab 2 are free when you add a tablet line on a qualifying plan.

Over at Metro by T-Mobile, the Galaxy A37 5G is free when you bring your number and join the $40 Period plan, and the activation fee is waived. Metro is also offering the Galaxy A16 5G, Galaxy A17 5G, and a Moto G on Us to new and existing customers adding a line on a qualifying plan. If you’d rather keep your phone, new Metro customers can get unlimited 5G data for $15 per month for the first three months, after which the price goes up to $25 per month with AutoPay.

T-Mobile’s 12 Days of Magenta also returns from December 1 to 12, with a new accessory deal each day in the T-Life app across charging, protection, gaming, and audio. Before that, you can get the Harman Kardon Onyx Studio 9 for $149.99 (50% off) with a free JBL Clip 5, the JBL PartyBox Encore Essential 2 for $199.99 ($130 off), and 25% off when you buy three or more essential accessories.

As usual with carrier deals, make sure you read the fine print. The phone discounts come as up to 36 monthly bill credits for well-qualified customers (24 for business accounts), and the credits stop if you cancel your account or pay off the device early, leaving you on the hook for the remaining balance.

A $35 device connection charge may also apply, and T-Mix promotions hold your Picks for the length of the deal, so changing your plan, lines, or Picks could affect them. You can compare these offers against our roundup of the best Black Friday phone deals before committing.

HUAWEI found guilty of conspiracy to steal trade secrets in the US

HUAWEI's latest guilty verdict could spell trouble for its smartphones well beyond the US.

•

Nov 24, 2026 — 11:02 PM ET

•

•

Rita El Khoury / Android Authority

Add Android Authority on Google:

Preferred Source

Google Discover

TL;DR

• Huawei has been found guilty of 10 of 12 criminal counts in a US trial, including conspiracy to steal trade secrets, bank fraud, and sanctions violations.

• The verdict adds another hurdle for Huawei as it continues to face US restrictions that have kept its smartphones out of the mainstream American market since 2019.

Chinese smartphone maker HUAWEI makes some of the best Android smartphones in the world. However, the company hasn’t been allowed to sell its devices in the US since its 2019 ban, when the Trump administration added the company to the US Commerce Department’s Entity List. That decision had a major impact on HUAWEI’s smartphone business, with Google subsequently delivering it another blow by barring the company from using its services for new devices.

Now, HUAWEI is facing another setback in its already strained relationship with the US. A federal jury in Brooklyn has found the company guilty of conspiring to steal trade secrets and defrauding banks, adding another complication to what was already looking like an uphill battle for its return to the American smartphone market.

Speaking with press before the Mate 90 launch earlier this year, HUAWEI’s Richard Yu had reportedly said that the company’s global phone share “was once number one,” but now, it only sell several million units of smartphones outside China every year. He had added that the company is “trying to return to the overseas market step by step.” However, this latest guilty verdict in the US could put a damper on HUAWEI’s global growth plans.

The jury found HUAWEI guilty on 10 of 12 criminal counts, including conspiracy to steal trade secrets, bank and wire fraud, and violations of US sanctions. Prosecutors accused the company of stealing intellectual property from American technology firms, including Cisco, Motorola, and T-Mobile, while also concealing business dealings in sanctioned countries such as Iran.

However, the jury acquitted the company of the more serious racketeering conspiracy charge and conspiracy to obstruct justice. HUAWEI has said it plans to appeal the convictions, but it could still end up facing billions of dollars in financial penalties during the sentencing.

In a statement issued after the verdict, Huawei wrote:

The five trade secret-related disputes cited by the government were all civil matters that were resolved over the past two decades. No court ever found HUAWEI liable for willful intellectual property misappropriation, and the company was never ordered to pay damages for trade secret misappropriation. We will thoroughly review the relevant verdicts and take all necessary legal actions to defend our rights and interests….HUAWEI takes its compliance obligations seriously. We remain focused on serving our customers and partners and ensuring continuous and stable business operations.

items.title: Google explains why your Nest camera is missing some features in the Home app
items.summary: No, Google Home's limited Nest camera controls aren't a bug.
items.body:

Smart home

Google explains why your Nest camera is missing some features in the Home app

No, Google Home's limited Nest camera controls aren't a bug.

•

Nov 24, 2026 — 10:28 PM ET

•

•

Edgar Cervantes / Android Authority

Add Android Authority on Google:

Preferred Source

Google Discover

TL;DR

• Google is clearing up confusion around the Nest-to-Google Home transition, explaining why some users only see a live camera feed without the usual controls.

• Nest cameras and doorbells that haven’t been transferred to Google Home won’t have access to features like event history, timeline scrubbing, and notifications.

• Users can manually transfer their cameras now by tapping “Get started” in Google Home or wait for Google’s automatic migration on January 25, 2027.

Google is finally putting an end to the Nest app on January 25, 2027, moving supported Nest devices into Google Home. This migration is part of Google’s broader effort to bring its smart home ecosystem under one roof. However, it seems there’s been some confusion as to how the migration will work.

Since Google’s announcement about retiring the Nest app, users trying to move to the Google Home app noticed that their cameras and doorbells weren’t showing all the features they expected. Now, Google has explained why this is the case.

According to the company, Nest cameras and doorbells that haven’t been transferred to Google Home won’t have access to features like event history, timeline scrubbing, and notifications.

Anish Kattukaran, Google’s Senior Director of Product Management for Home and Nest, addressed the issue in a post on X, explaining that users who see a limited camera interface likely haven’t transferred their devices from the Nest app to Google Home yet.

Google

Kattukaran says users should tap the “Get started” prompt to move their cameras over and unlock the full experience. Alternatively, they can simply wait for Google to automatically transfer their devices on January 25, 2027.

The clarification follows similar advice shared by the Google Nest community on Reddit. According to the community post, if your Nest camera or doorbell in Google Home only shows a live video stream but doesn’t offer event history, timeline scrubbing, or notifications, your device hasn’t completed the migration.

In other words, seeing a live feed in Google Home doesn’t necessarily mean your camera has been fully transferred to the app. You’ll need to complete the migration to get access to the full set of camera controls and features.

If you don’t want to wait until January, Google has also published instructions for manually transferring Nest cameras and doorbells to Google Home.

items.title: Tidal Bans AI Music, While Apple Music Sticks to Labels
items.summary: Streaming music service Tidal today said it plans to start blocking AI music on December 9. Any track generated entirely with AI will be removed from the platform, with Tidal rejecting AI songs in the future. Tidal lead Robert Andersen said 43 percent of tracks uploaded in the last 90 days have been…
items.body: Streaming music service Tidal today said it plans to start blocking AI music on December 9. Any track generated entirely with AI will be removed from the platform, with Tidal rejecting AI songs in the future. Tidal lead Robert Andersen said 43 percent of tracks uploaded in the last 90 days have been flagged as AI-generated. Approximately 29 million songs will be deleted and Tidal expects 80,000 to 85,000 songs to be rejected per day. AI music will start disappearing on December 9 and will be "completely gone" at the beginning of 2027. AI-assisted music will continue to be allowed, since the policy is only for songs made entirely with AI tools. Tidal previously demonetized AI music, but removing it goes a step further. Andersen said Tidal believes the move will "resonate with both artists and listeners alike" because 96 percent of AI songs get zero plays. Apple hasn't banned AI songs from Apple Music , but it introduced AI Transparency Tags earlier this year. Apple is relying on labels and distributors to disclose when AI has been used, and it said in August that tracks "materially generated using AI" must have a "Made With AI" label. In April, ‌Apple Music‌ VP Oliver Schusser said that more than a third of monthly uploads to ‌Apple Music‌ are 100 percent AI-generated, but AI music accounted for less than 0.5 percent of actual listening. items.title: Add Holiday Lights and Snow to Your Mac With Festivitas
items.summary: Festivitas is a fun little holiday-themed Mac app that developer Simon Støvring introduced two years ago and has been updating since. Its main purpose is to add lights to the Mac's Dock and menu bar, but there's also a version for the iPhone and iPad . The holiday 2026 Festivitas update adds new cus…
items.body: Festivitas is a fun little holiday-themed Mac app that developer Simon Støvring introduced two years ago and has been updating since. Its main purpose is to add lights to the Mac's Dock and menu bar, but there's also a version for the iPhone and iPad . The holiday 2026 Festivitas update adds new customizations. For the first time, you can upload custom bulb shapes. There's an option to import an image and convert it to a bulb in a string of lights. Simple PNGs on a transparent background produce the best results, and for more complex images, bulbs can use the original colors. You can customize light shapes, color, size, opacity, drop height, cable thickness, and more in the Settings. Lights can animate with different patterns, like pulse, twinkle, chase, and wave. There are pointer decorations like sparkles, bubbles, falling leaves, confetti, a Christmas tree, a wreath, and more. Falling snow will now pile up on top of app windows for an added holiday effect. You can adjust snow rate, density, and flake size. Snow and lights can be displayed above app windows or just on the desktop, with lights also visible on the Dock. Shortcuts can be used to play music and turn on lights, activate the snow effect if the weather forecast includes snow, and start a snowstorm. Along with custom bulb shapes and falling snow, Festivitas for the iPhone and ‌iPad‌ now fully transparent animated widgets on the without a screenshot workaround. Festivitas for Mac requires some accessibility access to work. I asked Støvring about Apple's planned permission changes in macOS 27.3, and how they will affect the Festivitas app. He said Festivitas gets far more access than it needs because Apple's options aren't granular enough, and he'd prefer to ask for less access. Menu bar lights, snow, and pointer effects work without the System & App Protection Override permission, while lights in the Dock and snow landing on windows require access. Festivitas for the Mac offers customer-chosen fair pricing

TL;DR

• Android Auto appears to be introducing a new UI for many apps, with navigation options stacked on the side of the screen.

• Compared to screen-top navigation, the new interface should be easier for drivers to access without being distracted.

• So far, we’ve seen this look with Spotify, YouTube Music, Amazon Music, and the system dialer.

For as much as we like a good UI on our phones, interface design is arguably even more important when we’re looking at a platform like Android Auto, and today we’re checking out what seems to be an intuitive new upgrade with a big emphasis on easy touch controls.

On Android Auto 18.2.664604-release, we’re starting to see apps adopt a new layout, trading screen-top navigation options for a list along the side. For an example, here’s how Spotify used to look:

Compare that with how the app is starting to appear for Android Auto users now:

Instead of having to stretch all the way across the screen to navigate within the app, all our options are conveniently lined up along one side. While that does result in some trade-offs in terms of the density of content on the display, what we do have left tends to be larger and makes better use of available space.

Beyond the new navigation layout, we also spot a few other small tweaks here, like a big new now-playing bar with album art and playback controls.

We see a similar transition happening for YouTube Music. Here’s what we’ve had so far:

AssembleDebug / Android Authority

And now the new, side-navigation layout:

Google Photos is forcing some Galaxy users to save every minor edit as a copy

TL;DR

• Google Photos is forcing some Samsung Galaxy users running One UI 9 to save even minor edits as separate copies.

• We’ve independently confirmed the absence of the regular Save option on a Galaxy S23 FE.

• Samsung has reportedly escalated the issue to its engineers, though it’s still unclear whether this is a bug or an intentional change.

Google Photos is forcing some Samsung Galaxy users to save images with simple edits, like minor crops, as their own copies. As you might expect, this is already causing frustration among users who are now stuck deleting unnecessary copies from their Google Photos libraries every time they make a minor adjustment to an image.

For reference, the app has traditionally allowed users to simply overwrite original images after minor edits have been made to them. The tech giant recently went as far as letting users overwrite original images even after advanced edits like Magic Eraser, Unblur, or edits with UltraHDR and C2PA formats. That’s precisely why the sudden disappearance of the regular Save option for basic edits is perplexing.

Users who have reported facing the bug all have one thing in common. They’re all Samsung users. We’ve spotted complaints across Reddit and the Google Support forum, with all affected users also suggesting that they’re on One UI 9. Reports about the simple save option’s absence first surfaced all the way back in September, but it wasn’t until earlier this month that we observed a significant uptick in complaints.

One user reported encountering the issue on their Samsung A35:

Just the other day I noticed while cropped a screenshot that I could only save the photo as a copy rather than the original photo itself… I thought it was a one time fluke, but when editing other photos later in the day I noticed the same behavior: all photos in the Google Photos gallery can ONLY “save as copy.”

A Z Fold 8 Ultra user expressed a similar frustration:

On my Fold8 Ultra (One UI 9, Android 17), after the “Updating Photo Editor” notification, Google Photos offers only “Save as copy” for every edit, even a simple crop.

A Galaxy S26 user took to the Google Support forum to complain:

Google Photos used to let me save a simple crop to the original photo. Now the editor only shows “Save as…” Why is Save no longer available, and how can I restore it without creating duplicate photos?

Note that users report the Save button’s absence in photos taken from the phone’s camera, screenshots, and images saved from the internet. I checked my Galaxy S23 FE, and I can confirm that the regular Save button is absent for me as well. Here’s what I’m seeing on my device:

After making a minor edit, Google Photos only offers a Save as copy option, with no regular Save button, not even in the three-dot menu, as seen in the screenshots above.

At the moment, it is unclear if this is a bug or an intended change. At least one user has confirmed that they’ve reported the issue to Samsung, and the company has reportedly passed the issue on to its engineers. We’ve also reached out to Samsung to confirm the same. We’ll update this article if and when we hear back.

TL;DR

• Anbernic has released a new showcase trailer for its upcoming RG DDS handheld.

• The video focuses on the hardware, colors, and features.

• It avoids naming any of the emulators installed on the device.

This has been the year for Nintendo 3DS clones. All colors of the Retroid Pocket Duo are now shipping, and Anbernic’s RG DDS will also start shipping in a couple of weeks. Speaking of the RG DDS, Anbernic has released a new trailer for the upcoming handheld. The trailer notably takes a different direction from previous videos.

In the new trailer, Anbernic focuses mainly on the hardware, colors, and features. We get shots of the handheld from different angles and close-ups that show off the build quality. As for the colors, you’ll have your choice between black, white, and blue. It also integrates over 30 gaming platforms and has a dedicated section for Android apps.

One can’t help but notice that the trailer appears to downplay the installed emulators compared to previous videos. There is footage of games being played toward the end of the video, but Anbernic refrains from mentioning the names of the emulators used.

Last month, Anbernic found itself in a bit of hot water after its last promotional video. In that video, the company showed off its own forked version of Azahar (a 3DS emulator) called “Azahar Plus.” That stunt prompted the Azahar team to pull its support from all Anbernic products going forward. It appears Anbernic decided to play it safe in its latest showcase.

However, Anbernic’s problems go deeper than beef with Azahar. Recently, the Entertainment Software Association (ESA) suggested that the US Trade Representative should add ANBERNIC to the “Notorious Markets” list. Being added to this list would prevent ANBERNIC from selling its handhelds in the US.

items.title: Google Says Apple's iOS Browser Rules Offer 'Choice on Paper, Not in Practice'
items.summary: Google's Chrome for Developers team today supported Mozilla's complaint about Apple's rules on non-WebKit browser engines in the European Union, calling out restrictions that make launching an alternative engine too difficult. Mozilla recently joined a coalition of up to 55,000 businesses and organi…
items.body: Google's Chrome for Developers team today supported Mozilla's complaint about Apple's rules on non-WebKit browser engines in the European Union, calling out restrictions that make launching an alternative engine too difficult. Mozilla recently joined a coalition of up to 55,000 businesses and organizations to ask the European Commission to force Apple to change its browser rules. Apple started allowing alternative browser engines in the EU in early 2024 , but the coalition says no browser maker has been able to transfer its EU users from Apple's WebKit engine to a new engine because of Apple's conditions. Mozilla explained that using its Gecko browser engine instead of WebKit would require releasing a second Firefox app. Apple says apps with alternative browser engines have to be distributed only in the EU, so Mozilla has been unable to add Gecko to its existing app. Firefox users in the EU would need to transfer to a new app and move all their content, and many users might not be willing to switch. Mozilla said Apple's conditions are "unworkable" and that Apple has only complied with the EU's Digital Markets Act "on paper." Chrome for Developers echoed the statement in its X post: We agree with @mozilla. Nearly 3 years after alternative browser engines on iOS were EU-mandated, zero launched due to remaining Apple restrictions. Forcing browsers to ship separate apps and re-acquire users is choice on paper, not in practice. Though one Google team expressed support for Mozilla, Google did not sign the open letter to the European Commission. In 2023, Google started work on an experimental version of Chromium for iOS with the Blink engine, but Google said it was only a prototype that would not be released. In June 2025, Mozilla and Apple participated in a DMA workshop where Mozilla brought up iOS support for third-party browser engines. Kindles are getting new life after being discontinued.

TL;DR

• Owners of old Kindles have found new life for them as DIY weather stations.

• After jailbreaking the devices, they’re vibe coding apps that display the weather and other information.

• As Amazon continues to end support for more Kindles, new uses for old Kindles are likely to become more popular.

There is magic in reading a book, but when the device you read it on is no longer useful, you can always conjure it into something entirely different — which is what’s happening right now on the Kindle Jailbreak sub on Reddit. Posters are showing off old Kindles that now act as weather stations thanks to jailbreaking and a little vibe coding.

One poster took their 7th-generation Kindle and used Claude for the transformation. They went to kindlemodding.org and followed a guide to jailbreak their device and then added the Kindle Unified Application Launcher (KUAL), an app launcher made for modded Kindles.

After that, they set the parameters for a weather station app with Claude. The Kindle is mounted on a wall and gets its data through Wi-Fi. The poster said the battery drain is only 10% per week because of power-saving measures they put in place. The app is set to update the data during the day at one-hour intervals, with the screen sleeping between updates. The Wi-Fi is on only when data is fetched.

The replies to the post turned up other people who found that their old Kindles also make for handy ways to check the weather, including a Pokémon-themed one that displays Pokédex entries alongside the time, date, and weather. One person said that they added news headlines to display next to the weather on theirs.

Some said they were now inspired to start similar projects. As one poster put it, “Kindles are amazing post-jailbreak. I’m wanting to use it all the time. Once you jailbreak it makes the thing come to life.”

Another post on the same sub showed what looked like a fourth-generation Kindle Touch with a vibe-coded weather station app. “Works much better than any cheap weather gadget I’ve ever owned,” its creator wrote.

Modifying Kindles has always been a thing, but the practice has picked up since Amazon announced in April that it would end support for older devices. This meant that not only would Kindles not get software and security updates, but they also could no longer download books from the Kindle Store. It was devastating news to people who had devices that were years old but still worked perfectly fine.

Just yesterday, Amazon added two other Kindles, the 10th-generation Kindle and the Kindle Paperwhite, to its end-of-life list for support, though it’s not clear yet if they will be able to access the Kindle Store.

Putting these still functioning E-Ink tablets to other uses is a great way to keep them out of landfills and still adding to daily life.

Being unable to use Google Maps in such a situation is not exactly ideal. Unfortunately, a bug is making that a reality for some Android Auto drivers.

Other times, the entire map area disappears, leaving an empty black screen. The issue is said to happen randomly, but can be fixed temporarily by clearing the cache in Google Maps and Android Auto and then restarting the phone.

A majority of the reports appear to come from owners of Ford vehicles. It’s unclear if the black screen problem is only happening in Ford vehicles or if other Android Auto users are also affected. items: Some Android Auto users are running into an issue with Google Maps.
The Maps app appears to fail to load, leaving a black screen.
The bug is being reported mostly by Ford vehicle owners.

blocks.text: Imagine you’re visiting an unfamiliar place and you’re ready to go home. However, when you pull up Google Maps to navigate your way back, there’s nothing there on the screen. Being unable to use Google Maps in such a situation is not exactly ideal. Unfortunately, a bug is making that a reality for some Android Auto drivers.

Several Android Auto users are reporting a strange issue with Google Maps. When booting up Android Auto, Google Maps appears to fail to load. As a result, users are seeing a black screen instead of the map that should be there. You can see an example of the issue in the picture immediately below.
u/Tunnynuke

The good news is that it sounds like there are a few solutions to the problem. One driver who ran into the same bug says they were able to fix the problem by waking their phone with a tap on the screen. Another claims they are able to temporarily fix the issue by tapping into zone lighting and then back to Android Auto.

Another Android Auto user shared a similar but slightly different problem. According to this driver, when Google Maps loads incorrectly, a black bar will sometimes take up part of the screen. Other times, the entire map area disappears, leaving an empty black screen. The issue is said to happen randomly, but can be fixed temporarily by clearing the cache in Google Maps and Android Auto and then restarting the phone.

A majority of the reports appear to come from owners of Ford vehicles. It’s unclear if the black screen problem is only happening in Ford vehicles or if other Android Auto users are also affected. Android Authority has reached out to Google for comment. We will update this article once new information becomes available.
